mainEntity.name: Is an EICR safety inspection mandatory before selling a property in Mold?

acceptedAnswer.text: While not legally mandatory for private home sellers, mortgage lenders and conveyancing solicitors in Flintshire increasingly request an up-to-date EICR. Having a satisfactory report avoids conveyancing delays and prevents buyers from negotiating price reductions due to outdated wiring.

mainEntity.name: What are the main warning signs that a property in Mold requires a consumer unit upgrade?

acceptedAnswer.text: Key indicators include old rewireable fuse boxes with cast-iron or wooden backings, lack of residual current device (RCD) protection, flickering lights, or scorched socket outlets. Upgrading to a modern metal RCBO board with Surge Protection (SPD) ensures full BS 7671 safety compliance.

mainEntity.name: What electrical regulations apply to private landlords in Flintshire under Welsh law?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under the Renting Homes (Wales) Act and electrical safety regulations, landlords must ensure fixed wiring is inspected at least every 5 years, accompanied by an EICR certificate. Landlords must also ensure working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms are hardwired on every floor.
